revise.statement: 3.2.0 merges RequestContext into AppContext (deprecated alias); an already-pushed app context is not reused when dispatching a request

12 Flask dispatch/error/teardown methods now take ctx: AppContext as first param; Flask.__init_subclass__ detects old-signature overrides, warns DeprecationWarning, wraps subclass method via remove_ctx and patches the base class via add_ctx
The old-signature compat shim (__init_subclass__) has zero direct test coverage; the only Flask-subclass method override test uses the new signature (test_subclassing.py:8)
evidence: grep across tests: no old-style overrides of the 12 patched methods in Flask subclasses
pytest filterwarnings=['error'] (pyproject.toml:109-111) makes the class-creation DeprecationWarning a hard error — no test can exercise it without pytest.warns

revise.statement: No test asserts the 'app context not reused when dispatching a request' behavior change (g isolation, per-request appcontext_pushed under nested app context)
evidence: grep tests for reuse/not-reused semantics; test_appctx.py/test_testing.py test list

revise.statement: Session is now loaded lazily on first access (not at context push); sessions.py open_session docstring still claims push-time loading; test_session_interface.py:8 still references removed RequestContext.match_request()
3.2.0 delta is essentially one architectural refactor (context merge + ctx-through-dispatch), 11 commits since 3.1.2, committed directly to main by one maintainer
Upstream status of Flask 3.2.0 (released or not, known regressions) could not be verified: web_fetch provider unavailable in this runtime; search snippets only
evidence: web_fetch errors: no usable web provider
web_search snippets for CHANGES.rst on main still show Version 3.2.0 unreleased

revise.statement: Ecosystem impact of context merge and dispatch signature change (extensions subclassing Flask with old signatures) is likely significant but unverified in this snapshot
evidence: known ecosystem pattern of Flask subclassing (researcher inference)
shim exists precisely because maintainers expect old-signature subclasses

hypotheses.statement: The most important problems in this snapshot are the untested and fragile old-signature compat shim and the under-tested breaking context-merge semantics, both concentrated in the single 3.2.0 refactor; the CRLF working tree is noise, not a change
